panels.text: 1686. Edward Lloyd opens a coffee house on Tower Street, a popular place for sailors, merchants and shipowners. He gives them reliable shipping news.
The shipping industry community gathers there to discuss maritime insurance, shipbroking and foreign trade.
In December 1691 the coffee house moves to Lombard Street, where Lloyd has a pulpit installed. From it, maritime auction prices and shipping news are announced.
The dealings there led to the establishment of the insurance market Lloyd's of London. In 1774 the participating members formed a committee and moved to the Royal Exchange as the Society of Lloyd's.
Lloyds Bank, however, is not named after the coffee house. It was founded in Birmingham by Sampson Lloyd.

probes.question: What did Edward Lloyd have installed in his Lombard Street coffee house to announce shipping news?
